cards.method: Small linear(ized) DSGE: Klein (2000) solution + Kalman-filter ML estimation, structural IRFs, forecasts and historical shock decomposition
cards.when: you have a SMALL linearized DSGE (log-linear equilibrium conditions with rational-expectations leads; e.g. a 3-equation New Keynesian or a linearized RBC model) and you want (a) to solve it at given parameters -> policy/transition matrices + saddle-path stability (dsge_solve), (b) to estimate the structural parameters on real observed macro data by ML through the Kalman filter (dsge_estimate), (c) structural IRFs to fundamental shocks (dsge_irf), (d) model-consistent forecasts (dsge_forecast), (e) a historical shock decomposition + smoothed structural shocks (dsge_shock_decomposition)
cards.when_not: a large or genuinely nonlinear DSGE, with occasionally binding constraints (that needs a higher-order perturbation solver — outside this linear-formula node); atheoretical multivariate forecasting -> #11-#15; a plain state-space model with no rational-expectations cross-equation restrictions -> #56-#61; a Bayesian DSGE with a random-walk Metropolis posterior (not exposed here); a shock count that differs from the observable count (the Klein solver requires equality)

alternatives.criterion: you want a general linear state-space model (local level or trend, unobserved components) WITHOUT rational-expectations cross-equation restrictions; the DSGE imposes theoretical restrictions that a plain state-space model does not
atheoretical reduced-form dynamics/forecasting without structural microfoundations; you do not want to impose equilibrium conditions
structural shocks + IRFs but with identification through restrictions on a VAR, not through the full DSGE cross-equation structure
you want posterior distributions/credible bands with priors (adaptive RWMH) rather than ML point estimates + delta-method SE

output_key_fields: dsge_solve: policy_matrix (G, controls×states); transition_matrix (H); shock_matrix (M); obs_matrix (D); eigenvalue_moduli + eigen_classification; stable (saddle path); n_stable/n_states; object=dsge_solution (register -> dsge_irf)

dsge_estimate: coefficients + se (the structural parameters + the log shock SD, delta method); loglik (Kalman); nobs; convergence (0=OK); stable; identification{identified,rank,condition_number,strength,summary}; the policy/transition matrices; object=dsge_fit (register)
dsge_irf: irf, a frame {period, impulse, response, value[, se, lower, upper]}; has_se (True only for an estimated fit); impulses/responses; source_class
dsge_forecast: forecasts {period,variable,value}; horizon; states (h×n_states); obs_matrix (h×n_obs); variables
dsge_shock_decomposition: decomposition_by_obs (per observable: T×{shocks..,initial}); obs_names; shock_names; observed (T×n_obs deviations); smoothed_shocks ((T-1)×n_shocks) + smoothed_shock_names
interpretation_traps: saddle-path stability is a PREREQUISITE: stable=False means the solution is neither unique nor stable (a Blanchard-Kahn violation) — do NOT interpret the impulse responses or forecasts; change the parameters or the specification
the number of exogenous state shocks MUST equal the number of observed controls (the Klein solver): the wrapper gates it explicitly (#state_eqs == #obs_eqs); fewer shocks -> stochastic singularity
lead(x) or E(x) in the formula is the rational-expectations forward term E_t[x_{t+1}], NOT a real future value; a state is always an exogenous AR process carrying a shock (shock=True)

standard errors on the impulse responses exist ONLY when the object is an estimated fit (the delta method on an estimated covariance); on a calibrated solution se is ignored and has_se=False — there is no sampling uncertainty at fixed parameters
dsge_forecast/dsge_shock_decomposition require a dsge_fit (they need Kalman-filtered/smoothed states from an estimation on data); a bare dsge_solve is not enough -> a hard gate

dsge_estimate: a non-zero convergence code, or an unidentified model, means the coefficients and standard errors are not reliable (a flat likelihood, or weak identification); check the condition number and the per-parameter strength before interpreting them
demean=True removes only the mean — the observables must already be stationary (log deviations); trending or unit-root data give a wrong likelihood
ML point estimates + delta-method SE (NOT Bayesian): for posterior uncertainty with priors you need the Bayesian node (bayes_dsge)
sources: Klein 2000 J. Economic Dynamics and Control 24(10) (using the generalized Schur form to solve a linear rational-expectations model)
Klein (2000) Using the generalized Schur form to solve a multivariate linear rational expectations model, J. Economic Dynamics & Control 24:1405
Sims (2002) Solving linear rational expectations models, Computational Economics 20:1
Herbst & Schorfheide (2016) Bayesian Estimation of DSGE Models, Princeton University Press (the Kalman-filter likelihood, identification)
Galí (2015) Monetary Policy, Inflation, and the Business Cycle, 2nd ed. (the three-equation New Keynesian model)
precondition_tools: dsge_solve (solve at the calibrated parameters FIRST; stable=True means the saddle path, so the model is solvable before you attempt estimation)
dsge_estimate (the ML fit; check that the convergence code is 0 and that the model is identified before interpreting the impulse responses or the forecasts)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (loading the observed macro series as a data_frame; the column names == the observed controls)
c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_adf_test (the observables must be stationary deviations — demean=True removes the mean, NOT a trend or a unit root)

cards.method: Structural simultaneous-equation macro-econometric model (FRB/US-style): MDL definition → estimate → deterministic/stochastic simulation → policy multipliers
cards.when: you have a structural system of simultaneous macro-model equations (behavioral equations with coefficients to estimate + accounting identities) defined in an MDL string; you want (a) coefficient estimation (OLS/IV) per equation, (b) deterministic/stochastic simulation or a forecast/scenario for the endogenous variables, (c) a table of policy multipliers (impact/interim/dynamic) of the endogenous variables with respect to exogenous instruments
cards.when_not: a single-equation model (single-equation OLS or IV -> category 07); a reduced-form VAR or VECM with no theoretical identities (-> categories 03/05); a micro-founded DSGE with rational expectations, Bellman equations and structural shocks (this card solves a backward-looking structural form, NOT a general rational-expectations DSGE); you do not have data covering ALL the variables over the estimation and simulation period

alternatives.criterion: you want a projection/scenario (DYNAMIC/FORECAST) or a stochastic simulation of the endogenous variables after estimation
you want impact/interim/dynamic policy multipliers (endogenous targets with respect to exogenous instruments)
a single-equation causal estimate with an endogenous regressor (not a whole system)
reduced-form dynamics without theoretical identities/behavioral restrictions
a micro-founded rational-expectations DSGE (structural shocks, IRFs) rather than a backward-looking structural form

output_key_fields: sem_estimate: coefficients (a named list per behavioral equation: named numeric); statistics (RSquared/AdjustedRSquared/DurbinWatson/Fstatistics/SER/AIC/BIC/LogLikelihood per behavioral equation); residuals (a series per behavioral equation); endogenous/exogenous/behaviorals/identities; estTech; object (the registry handle)
sem_simulate (deterministic): mode='deterministic'; simulation (a named list of ts per endogenous variable); simType; simAlgo; tsrange
sem_simulate (stochastic): mode='stochastic'; sim_mean & sim_sd (a named list of ts per endogenous variable); stoch_replica; seed
sem_multipliers: multiplier_matrix (a TARGET×INSTRUMENT matrix with var_period axis labels); target_labels (row labels); instrument_labels (column labels); tsrange
interpretation_traps: the data must extend AT LEAST one period before the start of the estimation or simulation whenever the equations contain a lag operator (otherwise a clean stop; the raw routine gives a cryptic error)
simulation, stochastic simulation and the multiplier matrix all require an estimated model with no blank coefficients; the node gates them, so an unestimated model is blocked

in the multipliers: when the INSTRUMENT period is later than the TARGET period the cell is 0 (causality does not run backwards); a single-period TSRANGE => impact multipliers, a multi-period one => interim/dynamic multipliers

stochastic=True adds an automatic normal disturbance with the regression standard error, ONLY in the behavioural equations and never in the identities; the seed is mandatory for reproducibility (default 2025)
FORECAST vs DYNAMIC: FORECAST uses simulated values for the lagged endogenous variables AND beyond the historical data; STATIC uses the actual lagged values — do not confuse them

estTech='IV' requires IV expressions inside the model definition, or in the iv argument; otherwise the routine errors (blocked); the Chow test, PDL, restrictions and automatic error structure are all declared INSIDE the model-definition string
sources: Brayton & Tinsley 1996 (a guide to FRB/US: a macroeconometric model of the United States)
Klein, L. (1950) 'Economic Fluctuations in the United States 1921–1941', Cowles Commission Monograph 11 (Klein Model I, the reference model)
Pindyck, R.S. & Rubinfeld, D.L. (1998) 'Econometric Models and Economic Forecasts', 4th ed., McGraw-Hill (structural simultaneous-equation estimation & simulation, multipliers)
Fair, R.C. (1984) 'Specification, Estimation, and Analysis of Macroeconometric Models', Harvard University Press (FRB/US-style structural macro modelling)
precondition_tools: c00_data_utilities/series_layout_conversion.ts_convert (a long frame -> a wide multi-series frame; one column per model variable)
sem_estimate (the PRODUCER: the estimated BIMETS_MODEL handle -> sem_simulate/sem_multipliers)

cards.method: Computable/Applied General Equilibrium — a structural dynamic model (sdm) with a Leontief/Cobb-Douglas/CES demand structure; equilibrium prices, activity levels, growth rate
cards.when: you have a technology/demand structure in IO/SAM form (a demand-coefficient matrix A, or Cobb-Douglas/CES shares Beta+alpha[+sigma]) + a supply matrix B + exogenous supplies S0Exg (labour/capital/off-network); you want to COMPUTE the general equilibrium — relative prices p (a numeraire), activity/output levels z, the demand matrix A·diag(z), the growth rate (in a purely productive economy); a fixed point (the Li structural dynamic model / a Sraffa system); optionally the time paths of the price adjustment towards equilibrium (ts=True)
cards.when_not: you want a linearized DSGE with rational expectations, impulse responses or Bayesian estimation on data (-> #200); stock-flow-consistent macro accounting with behavioural equations (-> #203); econometric structural macro-model estimation and simulation (-> #201); you have time series and want a regression or forecast rather than a calibrated general equilibrium; the multi-money, policy-experiment and intertemporal-path features are outside the curated surface

alternatives.criterion: you want a linearized rational-expectations DSGE (policy functions, IRFs, forecast, shock decomposition) rather than a calibrated Walrasian GE on an IO/SAM structure
stock-flow-consistent macro accounting with behavioral equations & balance-sheet consistency rather than market-clearing GE
an econometric structural macro model (estimated equations + multipliers) rather than a calibrated GE
you want price-responsive demand with a tunable elasticity of substitution (sigma) — CD is the special limit sigma->0

output_key_fields: p / p_normalized: the equilibrium prices (an n-vector) & the same normalised to the commodity-1 numeraire (p/p[1]; ONLY relative prices are meaningful)
z: the equilibrium levels of activity/output/utility (an m-vector)
demand_matrix: A_eq %*% diag(z) — the demand matrix at equilibrium (chart-data); S: the supply matrix of the initial period
A_eq: the equilibrium demand-coefficient matrix (for CD/CES it differs from the inputs — it is computed at the equilibrium prices)
growth_rate: the endogenous equilibrium growth rate (a purely productive economy with no exogenous supply; blank otherwise)
tolerance / tolCond / converged: the convergence error against the threshold; converged=True exactly when tolerance<=tolCond
ts_p/ts_z/ts_S/ts_q (only with ts=True): the adjustment paths of the prices, levels, supply and sales rate in the last iteration
interpretation_traps: ONLY relative prices: a GE determines prices up to scale; ALWAYS use p_normalized (numeraire=commodity 1); the absolute p values are arbitrary
converged=False means the solution is NOT an equilibrium (tolerance>tolCond); raise maxIteration or check the structure; the node is stateless, so there is no silent retry
CD requires every column of Beta to sum to 1 (Cobb-Douglas shares); CES does NOT (non-negative shares suffice); the wrapper gates it
CES sigma: the elasticity parameter (sigma<0 is usual; sigma->0 => the Cobb-Douglas limit, sigma->-inf => Leontief); it is NOT the elasticity of substitution 1/(1-sigma) — do not confuse them
S0Exg: blank means an endogenous commodity, a non-zero value an exogenous supply (labour, land); 0 is FORBIDDEN, and the wrapper blocks it
dstype='constant' = price-INDEPENDENT demand (Leontief/Sraffa); CD/CES = price-responsive (A is recomputed at every iteration); a different economic interpretation
maxIteration=1 gives a pure dynamic simulation rather than an equilibrium computation; combine it with ts=True for the adjustment paths
sources: LI Wu (2019, ISBN 9787521804225) General Equilibrium and Structural Dynamics: Perspectives of New Structural Economics; LI Wu (2010) A Structural Growth Model and its Applications to Sraffa's System (IIOA 18th conf.)
Torres, Jose L. (2016, ISBN 9781622730452) Introduction to Dynamic Macroeconomic General Equilibrium Models (2nd ed.), Vernon Press
Varian, Hal R. (1992, ISBN 0393957357) Microeconomic Analysis, W. W. Norton — general equilibrium, p.352
precondition_tools: cge_solve (constant demand first as a Leontief/Sraffa baseline; then CD/CES for price-responsive demand)
c00_data_utilities/canonical_disk_format.arw_read_parquet (loading the IO/SAM demand/supply matrices A/B/S0Exg from Parquet)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (alternatively: loading the coefficient matrices from CSV)

cards.method: Stock-Flow-Consistent (Godley-Lavoie) macro simulation — a baseline steady-state solve, policy scenarios (shocks), balance-sheet/transactions-flow accounting validation
cards.when: you have a THEORETICALLY SPECIFIED SFC model (a system of accounting identities + behavioral equations in the Godley-Lavoie tradition) and you want to SOLVE it to a steady state (sfc_simulate), to run policy scenarios with shocks to exogenous variables/parameters (sfc_scenario_run), and to VERIFY that the balance-sheet/transactions-flow matrix is water-tight (sfc_balance_check). A deterministic simulation with block-ordered Gauss-Seidel/Broyden/Newton root solving.
cards.when_not: you want to ESTIMATE parameters from data (SFC is calibrated/theory-driven, not estimated — go to an econometric structural model); you want a micro-founded DSGE with rational expectations/optimisation & log-linearization (a different paradigm); you have a single behavioral equation (run a regression, cat. 07/08); you want a stochastic/Monte Carlo ensemble or a sensitivity sweep (sfcr_multis/sfcr_random — deliberately outside the deterministic node)

alternatives.criterion: you want a counterfactual/policy shock (e.g. higher government spending, a higher tax rate) on an already solved baseline
you want to certify that the accounting identities close (every column/row of the TFM/BS sums correctly; locating a leak)
you want an ESTIMATED structural macro-econometric model (Klein type) with simulation/multiplier analysis rather than a calibrated SFC model
you want empirically identified shocks & IRFs from data rather than a theory-driven counterfactual

output_key_fields: sfc_simulate: paths (a data_frame period × all the variables; chart-data); steady_state (the values of the last period); variables/n_variables; method; converged; object (the baseline sfcr_tbl handle -> scenario/balance)
sfc_scenario_run: paths (the scenario data_frame; chart-data); final_values; shocked_vars; shock_start/shock_end; object (the scenario sfcr_tbl handle)

sfc_balance_check: consistent (a boolean; True means water-tight); leaking_rows/leaking_cols (the names that leak); max_row_residual/max_col_residual (the largest absolute accounting residual); row_residual_by_period/col_residual_by_period (chart data); plus a message
interpretation_traps: the underlying validation returns NO value — it either prints 'Water tight!' or aborts; the wrapper traps that into a consistent flag with the leaking rows and columns, AND computes explicit numeric residuals per period, which would otherwise never surface
SFC is calibrated/theory-driven, NOT estimated; the parameters (alpha1, theta,..) are given exogenously — do not 'estimate' them; the steady state depends on them (e.g. SIM: Y* = G/theta)

in growth models, where the stocks increase perpetually, the hidden equation and the validation must use a relative tolerance (rhtol=True) rather than an absolute one — otherwise computational buildup produces a spurious failure
the hidden equation (a redundant identity, e.g. Hh=Hs in SIM): if supplied, it is checked; its failure = a mis-specified model (a leak in the logic)

the scenario INHERITS the block structure & the final state from the baseline; a shock applied BEFORE the baseline has converged produces a transient that is not a policy effect; run the baseline for enough periods (~50+) first

sfcr_matrix rows: the first element = the row name, the rest are name-value pairs per code; do NOT add a manual 'sum' column to a TFM (it is generated automatically); in a BS the non-zero rows need an explicit 'Sum' column

a large max_col_residual or max_row_residual alongside consistent=True is impossible within tol; consistent=False with small residuals means the tolerance should be raised (stationary against growth models)
sources: Godley & Lavoie 2007, Monetary Economics: An Integrated Approach to Credit, Money, Income, Production and Wealth

Godley W. & Lavoie M. (2007) Monetary Economics: An Integrated Approach to Credit, Money, Income, Production and Wealth, Palgrave Macmillan (the SIM/PC/.. models, transactions-flow & balance-sheet matrices, water-tight accounting)

Kinsella S. & OShea T. (2010) Solution and Simulation of Large Stock Flow Consistent Monetary Production Models via the Gauss Seidel Algorithm, SSRN, doi:10.2139/ssrn.1729205 (the Gauss-Seidel method, cited in the sfcr_baseline help)
Peressini A.L., Sullivan F.E., Uhl J.J. (1988) The Mathematics of Nonlinear Programming, Springer (the Broyden & Newton-Raphson algorithms, cited in the sfcr_baseline help)
precondition_tools: sfc_simulate (solve the baseline FIRST; sfc_scenario_run & sfc_balance_check REQUIRE a solved sfcr_tbl handle)
sfc_scenario_run (a scenario = baseline + shock; it needs the baseline object)
sfc_balance_check (run it AFTER simulate/scenario to certify accounting consistency — a water-tight check)

cards.method: Sequence-space Jacobian: HANK, Krusell-Smith and RBC
cards.when: solving and estimating heterogeneous-agent general-equilibrium models fast enough to do policy analysis, by working with sequence-space Jacobians
cards.when_not: the model has no heterogeneity, where standard perturbation is simpler; occasionally binding constraints matter and the linearisation fails

alternatives.criterion: representative agent
heterogeneous agents, linearised transitions
occasionally binding constraints

output_key_fields: steady_state: the computed steady state
jacobians: the sequence-space Jacobians of each block
irf: linear impulse responses of aggregates and distributions
convergence: whether the steady state and the transition solved
interpretation_traps: THE STEADY STATE MUST SOLVE ACCURATELY FIRST; Jacobians computed around an inaccurate steady state are wrong in ways that look like economics
the method linearises the transition, so it cannot represent occasionally binding constraints or large nonlinear responses
grid choices for the idiosyncratic state materially affect aggregate Jacobians and must be checked for robustness
sources: Auclert, Bardoczy, Rognlie & Straub 2021 (Econometrica 89:2375-2408)
Kaplan, Moll & Violante 2018 (American Economic Review 108:697)
sequence-jacobian

cards.when: distributional macro questions -- wealth inequality, marginal propensities to consume, who a policy reaches -- need a solved household problem, not a representative agent
cards.when_not: aggregate dynamics alone are the question; the model's calibration cannot be disciplined by any available micro data

alternatives.criterion: distribution is irrelevant
prices are exogenous
prices must clear markets

output_key_fields: policy_functions: consumption and saving rules over the state space
distribution: the stationary wealth distribution
mpc: marginal propensities to consume, by wealth
aggregates: implied aggregate consumption and wealth
interpretation_traps: THE MPC DISTRIBUTION IS THE MODEL'S MAIN TESTABLE IMPLICATION and is very sensitive to the calibration of the income process and the borrowing constraint
a stationary distribution requires enough simulation or a fine enough grid; a truncated grid silently caps the top of the wealth distribution
partial and general equilibrium give very different policy answers because prices move in the latter
sources: Carroll 1997 (Quarterly Journal of Economics 112:1-55)
Aiyagari 1994 (Quarterly Journal of Economics 109:659)
Carroll, Kaufman, Kazil, Palmer & White 2018 (Econ-ARK)
econ-ark

cards.when: the primitives every dynamic model needs -- discretising a continuous shock, solving a linear-quadratic problem, running a Kalman filter on a state space
cards.when_not: the model's own solver provides these internally and you have no reason to override them

alternatives.criterion: the standard, though poor for persistent processes
far better for highly persistent processes
the problem is naturally discrete

output_key_fields: states, transition: the discretised Markov chain
policy, value: the solution of a dynamic program
moments: the discretisation's implied persistence and variance against the target
solution_diagnostics: convergence of the solver
interpretation_traps: TAUCHEN'S METHOD IS POOR FOR HIGHLY PERSISTENT PROCESSES -- with an autoregressive coefficient near 0.99 it badly understates persistence; Rouwenhorst matches it exactly and should be the default there
the number of grid points trades accuracy against speed and materially changes aggregate results in heterogeneous-agent models
always check the discretised chain's implied moments against the continuous process it replaces
sources: Tauchen 1986 (Economics Letters 20:177-181)
Rouwenhorst 1995, Asset pricing implications of equilibrium business cycle models (Frontiers of Business Cycle Research)
Kopecky & Suen 2010 (Review of Economic Dynamics 13:701)
quantecon

cards.method: Nonlinear perfect-foresight models with occasionally binding constraints
cards.when: the lower bound on interest rates, a borrowing constraint or an irreversibility binds sometimes, and a linear solution cannot represent that
cards.when_not: no constraint binds over the relevant range, where linearisation is fine and far faster

alternatives.criterion: no binding constraints
one constraint, occasionally binding
several constraints or large nonlinearity

output_key_fields: path: the nonlinear transition path
binding_periods: when each constraint bound
converged: whether the shooting or Newton solve converged
linear_comparison: the linear path, for reference
interpretation_traps: THE PATH IS STATE DEPENDENT: the response to a shock depends on where the economy starts and how large the shock is, so a single impulse response does not characterise the model
perfect foresight means agents know the whole future path, which is a strong assumption precisely when constraints bind
non-convergence is common near the constraint and a returned path must be checked, not assumed
sources: Guerrieri & Iacoviello 2015 (Journal of Monetary Economics 70:22-38)
Boehl 2022 (Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control 143:104523)
econpizza

cards.method: Perturbation DSGE solution and Bayesian estimation from a model file
cards.when: solving and estimating a structural macro model written down as equations, which is the standard workflow of policy institutions
cards.when_not: the model has strong nonlinearity that perturbation cannot capture; the data are too short to identify the structural parameters

alternatives.criterion: linear dynamics, fast, the usual default
risk and volatility effects matter
you want posteriors rather than a calibration

output_key_fields: solution: the policy and transition functions
posterior: parameter draws, where estimated
identification: which parameters the data can actually pin down
blanchard_kahn: whether the solution exists and is unique
interpretation_traps: THE BLANCHARD-KAHN CONDITIONS DECIDE WHETHER A SOLUTION EXISTS AT ALL -- indeterminacy or no solution is a property of the parameters, and a solver that returns something anyway is misleading
many DSGE parameters are weakly identified by the data; the posterior then reproduces the prior, which must be checked rather than assumed away
first-order solutions are certainty equivalent, so risk premia are identically zero and cannot be studied at that order
sources: Blanchard & Kahn 1980 (Econometrica 48:1305-1311)
Smets & Wouters 2007 (American Economic Review 97:586)
An & Schorfheide 2007 (Econometric Reviews 26:113)
gEconpy

cards.when: solving a linear rational-expectations system directly, when you have the equations in matrix form rather than a model file
cards.when_not: the system is nonlinear; you want estimation rather than a solution

alternatives.criterion: general, handles singular systems
the standard alternative with the same coverage
the system is non-singular and simpler

output_key_fields: policy_function: the solved decision rule
transition: the state transition
existence, uniqueness: the determinacy verdict
simulated: simulated paths where requested
interpretation_traps: A SINGULAR SYSTEM BREAKS THE BLANCHARD-KAHN METHOD but not the QZ methods; choosing the wrong solver produces a spurious 'no solution' verdict
the count of explosive eigenvalues against forward-looking variables is what decides determinacy, and it must be reported
the solution is certainty equivalent, so simulated moments contain no risk premia
sources: Klein 2000 (Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control 24:1405-1423)
Sims 2002 (Computational Economics 20:1)
linearsolve

cards.when: the model is an accounting-consistent system of stocks and flows, where every financial asset is somebody's liability
cards.when_not: the model is optimisation based with forward-looking agents; accounting consistency is not the organising principle

alternatives.criterion: monetary and financial accounting must close
feedback structure is the focus
optimisation and expectations are the focus

output_key_fields: solution: the simulated stocks and flows
accounting_check: whether every balance sheet and transaction matrix closes
steady_state: the long-run position, where one exists
convergence: solver convergence per period
interpretation_traps: THE ACCOUNTING CHECK IS THE MODEL'S MAIN VALIDATION: a non-zero residual in the transaction-flow matrix means the model is wrong, not merely imprecise
these models have no optimising agents, so behavioural equations are assumptions rather than derived; their parameters are not structural in the Lucas sense
results are sensitive to the closure -- which variable adjusts to clear each market -- and the closure must be stated
sources: Godley & Lavoie 2007, Monetary Economics: An Integrated Approach to Credit, Money, Income, Production and Wealth
Sterman 2000, Business Dynamics
pysolve3

cards.method: Agent-based macro and stock-flow-consistent ABM simulation
cards.when: heterogeneity, interaction and out-of-equilibrium dynamics are the subject, and no aggregation into a representative agent is defensible
cards.when_not: the question is about equilibrium comparative statics; the model cannot be calibrated against any observable

alternatives.criterion: you want equilibrium with heterogeneity
interaction and disequilibrium dynamics matter
aggregate feedback without agent detail

output_key_fields: simulated: agent-level and aggregate time series
aggregates: emergent macro variables
ensemble: results across seeds, which is the only honest summary
calibration_fit: distance from targeted moments
interpretation_traps: A SINGLE RUN OF AN AGENT-BASED MODEL IS ONE DRAW, not a result; every reported quantity must be an ensemble statistic across seeds
these models have many free parameters and can be made to produce almost any pattern; the calibration discipline is what makes them evidence
emergent regularities can be artefacts of the interaction topology or the update order rather than of the economics
sources: Tesfatsion & Judd 2006, Handbook of Computational Economics 2
Caiani et al. 2016 (Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control 69:375-408)
mesa

arguments.name: model
arguments.description: MDL model-string (MODEL... END· behaviorals with EQ>/COEFF>, identities with EQ>).

arguments.name: data
arguments.description: Handle to an panel (one column per variable)· covers ALL the vendog ∪ vexog of the model.

arguments.name: tsrange
arguments.description: Optional estimation period [startYear,startPeriod,endYear,endPeriod] (default = the TSRANGE of the MDL).

arguments.name: estTech
arguments.description: Estimation technique· OLS (default) or IV (Instrumental Variables).

arguments.name: iv
arguments.description: Character vector of instrumental-variables expressions (when estTech='IV' & they are not defined in the MDL).

arguments.name: eqList
arguments.description: Names of behavioral equations to estimate (default = all).

arguments.name: object
arguments.description: Handle to an estimated BIMETS_MODEL (from sem_estimate).

arguments.name: target
arguments.description: Endogenous target variables (⊆ vendog) for the multipliers.

arguments.name: instrument
arguments.description: Exogenous instrument variables (⊆ vexog) that are perturbed.

arguments.name: mm_shock
arguments.description: Relative perturbation of the instruments for the numerical computation (default 1e-5).

arguments.name: simType
arguments.description: Simulation type behind the multiplier matrix (default DYNAMIC).

arguments.name: object
arguments.description: Handle to an estimated BIMETS_MODEL (from sem_estimate).

arguments.name: simAlgo
arguments.description: Solution algorithm of the system (default GAUSS-SEIDEL).

arguments.name: stochastic
arguments.description: False=deterministic SIMULATE· True=STOCHSIMULATE (auto NORM(0,SER) perturbation per behavioral -> mean/sd).

arguments.name: stoch_replica
arguments.description: Number of stochastic replications when stochastic=True (>=2).

arguments.name: seed
arguments.description: Reproducibility seed for the stochastic path (StochSeed).

arguments.name: simConvergence
arguments.description: Convergence tolerance of the simulation (positive number· default 1e-5).

arguments.name: dstype
arguments.description: Demand structure: constant (Leontief/Sraffa constant A) | CD (Cobb-Douglas) | CES (default constant).

arguments.name: A
arguments.description: Handle to a demand-coefficient n-by-m matrix (non-negative)· ONLY for dstype=constant.

arguments.name: Beta
arguments.description: Handle to a share n-by-m matrix (non-negative)· required for CD/CES· CD => each column sums to 1.

arguments.name: alpha
arguments.description: Efficiency m-vector (CD/CES)· of length 1 (recycle) or m· default rep(1,m).

arguments.name: sigma
arguments.description: CES elasticity m-vector· of length 1 or m· required for dstype=CES.

arguments.name: Theta
arguments.description: Handle to a positive n-by-m matrix (CES scale params)· optional.

arguments.name: B
arguments.description: Handle to a supply-coefficient n-by-m matrix· default diag(n) (requires m==n).

arguments.name: S0Exg
arguments.description: Handle to an exogenous supply n-by-m (NA=endogenous, NOT 0)· default all NA.

arguments.name: z0
arguments.description: Initial activity levels m-vector (>0)· default rep(100,m).

arguments.name: GRExg
